_about: The narration of the two walkthrough films: one line per step of each film (the steps are the films' own burnt-in captions, from the recorder's events.json, plus the opening and closing cards). 'text' is what the captions file shows; 'say' (when given) is how the voice should say it; 'rate' is the voice's speed (0.5 normal); 'lead' is how long after the step begins the voice starts (default 0.3 s). 'check' is the start of the film's own caption for that step, so a line can never land on the wrong step. 'until' and 'gap' (closing cards only): the card has faded out by 'until' (from the recorder's frames: Field 170.46 s, Atlas 167.80 s) and nothing follows it, so the line may end right there.

lines.text: Chernozem Field, on a farm in Ukraine.
The overview shows the latest pass, what needs doing, and your fields.
Every clear Sentinel-2 pass is read, and the latest date is at the top.
Press a tile to pick out those fields in the list on the right.
The farm's weather, and whether rain is coming.
Fields shows every field on the satellite map, tinted by its condition. Pick one, or step through them with the arrows.
Its water, plant health, stress and harvest readiness.
This season's plant health against normal years.
Data shows the field's record since 2019, against the farm and normal years. The red line marks the full-scale invasion.
Hover, or use the arrow keys, to read any month's numbers.
Switch between plant health and water.
Download the outlines, passes and history, or the season report.
Back on the overview, tell us what happened: choose what it was and which field, write what you saw and when, and add a photo.
Press Send. Your words stay on screen while the report is saved.
The report opens the assistant, with the field and the photo.
It stays with the chat, beside the farm's readings.
The assistant answers from the farm's own readings, its history, and the weather.
Here is a saved conversation: how a field did this season, and what to watch.
Settings holds the farm's name and place, its fields, and their crops.
Set a crop by picking what you sowed. Until then, the detected crop is used.
To add a field, press Add a field, then click its corners on the satellite map.
The new field is saved, and analysed at once.
To remove a field, press its bin and confirm. Its readings go with it.
Choose hectares, acres or mu, and the whole app uses them.
lines.say: Choose hectares, acres, or moo, and the whole app uses them.

lines.text: Change farm is how you find your land: search for a village, paste coordinates, or draw it on the map.
The map flies there, and the fields around the pin are found.
Pick the fields that are yours, or select them all, then save.
Come back after each satellite pass.
Register at chernozem.app and read your own fields.
lines.say: Register at chernozem dot app and read your own fields.

lines.text: Chernozem Atlas: how an office uses it.
The totals for cropland, black soil, damage and people.
Where to start: the map, coloured by priority, and the top areas below.
Pick any analysed month. The Atlas runs again every month, by itself.
Switch between near term and post-crisis: two ways to rank the same land.
Next steps are worked out from the data. Tick them off as your team goes.
Type a budget to see what it covers.
The map shows priority square by square, with each state's name and border. The darker the green, the higher the priority.
Colour the map by value, by damage, by feasibility, or all three together.
Macro ranks whole states. Micro shows every square.
Satellite only shows the land itself, under the squares.
Move the weights, and the map and the top areas change at once.
The feasibility cutoff leaves out the hardest land to reach, for now, with a soft edge.
A place's scores, soil, and cost.
Data shows every analysed month. Hover over a bar for its numbers.
Switch between heavily damaged land, new damage, and people, month by month.
Compare two months: what changed, and the squares that changed most.
The report puts it on one page: the totals, the top ten places, the settings, and this month's alerts.
Save it as a PDF for donors.
Ask the assistant about any place. It answers from the same numbers as the map.
Here is a saved conversation about one of the top areas.
Settings holds the areas, the crisis, the data, and the team.
To add a new area, choose a country or region, type GPS coordinates, or draw a shape. Here, Moldova.
The last twelve months are analysed, and the area joins the list and the map.
The team: who can see this area, and who can change it.
And the crisis, if there is one.
Register at chernozem.app and rank your own region.
lines.say: Register at chernozem dot app and rank your own region.
